instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In the quiz report, write that I earned the trophy. 'The questions suited Pat' isn't an account of how I won.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There were twelve bird questions. You keep birds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I studied them for six months. Put the preparation before the score, please; keeping a cage doesn't answer questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody else knew it would be a bird round.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither did I. Write 'Pat's six months of study paid off'. Please don't replace the work with 'lucky' just because you didn't see me doing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please describe my race win as earned. Start with the finish order, not a theory about everyone being kind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They slowed down near the end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then record that I maintained my pace. Slowing isn't the same as giving someone a win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One of them stopped to tie a shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I checked my laces before the start. Put that under preparation, please. Don't turn a check I remembered into a gift somebody gave me.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You lost the chess game. Wash the dishes as agreed, please; glasses first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we were joking about the washing-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You pointed out the greasy pan when you had my queen. Please apply the same terms now I've checkmated you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we play again for double or nothing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After this load. Dry your hands before touching the pieces; I won't let another wager replace one you haven't settled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plan exceeded the budget. You agreed to announce the cut; I'll check your wording before the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only went over by two hundred pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say two hundred, not 'only'. Start with what the cut removes; people need the consequence before your explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You know how to say it. Could you make the announcement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll mark the pauses on your copy. Your name stays beside 'presenter'. Read me the first sentence now; we can correct it before you face them.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How are you scoring my picnic against last year's? Please show me the measure before calling it a success.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Attendance. If we beat last year, I get the larger events budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then separate attendance from satisfaction. What was last year's count, and where does mine stand?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Eighty last year, seventy today. But yours ran in the rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same counting method? Staff included both times? Please check before adjusting for weather; I need to know whether I'm ten behind or you're short of your budget target.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I ask for your vote, how are you ranking me against your cousin for club president? Give me a criterion, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Competence. He'll finally get our car park resurfaced.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a project, not a measure. Which part of my proposal puts me behind him?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You budgeted for next year. He says he'll do it now; my van's taking a beating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then score timing separately from cost. If I bring the work forward without raising fees, do I draw level? Tell me where that leaves your vote.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Enter on My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit them into your side of a contest or bargain before the stakes become fully clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put on our blue quiz badge before the final-round briefing. I'll make sure you're registered correctly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens to the losing team?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Team consequences come after registration. Name first, badge second; please don't skip ahead in the briefing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just cheer for you. I don't need a badge for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll list you as support. Supporters wear blue too; stand with us while I give the organizer our names. We'll cover the final-round duties together.

beats.text: Back my fete stall as joint entrant. Sign on this line; I'll handle the rest of the form.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's make this chess game decide who cooks all weekend. Write down the meals before we start, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed on a biscuit. I might actually enjoy cooking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then cooking isn't the whole stake. Add shopping and washing-up; we need an outcome neither of us can shrug off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll risk Saturday breakfast. Nothing more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Breakfast for both, including the dishes. Please write both names; one piece of toast for yourself won't settle this. Will you agree to that package?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your club captaincy on our rematch. I'll put up my coaching post. Let's specify the handover before we play.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why risk our jobs? Pride should be enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've forgotten six results played for pride. Please choose a consequence we have to act on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One training session. The loser sets out the cones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make it the rest of the season. One session can be called a favor; a season goes on the rota. Shall I put both names against that agreement?
